补充（读物外）：“人是万物的尺度”最早是古希腊哲学家普罗泰戈拉（**Protagoras**）的名言；罗素原书写的是 man is the measure of all things、truth is man-made，课程 PDF 改成了中性的说法。“空间和时间是心灵的性质”让人想到康德（**Kant**）一派的观点；“共相”指许多东西共有的性质和关系（比如“白”“在……之北”），罗素在原书第 9–10 章讨论，这份节选没有解释。

prompt.en: Objection: 'Russell says contemplation enlarges the Self. So isn't his reason for studying philosophy really a selfish one?'
prompt.zh: 反驳：“罗素说沉思能扩大自我，那他学哲学的理由不还是自私的吗？”

answer.en: No. Russell says the enlargement of the Self is best achieved when it is not directly sought, when only the desire for knowledge is at work. What blocks growth is self-assertion, which treats the world as a means to the Self's ends. In contemplation we start from the not-Self and adapt ourselves to what we find, so the Self grows only as a side effect of caring about something larger than itself.
answer.zh: 不是。罗素说自我的扩大最好是不刻意去求的（第 4 页）：只让求知的愿望起作用。阻碍自我成长的，正是自我主张，也就是把世界当成满足自己目的的工具（第 5 页）。沉思从非我出发，让自己去适应世界；自我的扩大，只是关心比自己更大的东西时附带的结果。

items.zh: 要塞里的守军（**garrison**）说的是本能式的、只顾私利的生活，不是哲学的生活。
items.en: The garrison is the instinctive life, not the philosophic life.

items.zh: 哲学的沉思是逃出去的“一条路”（**one way**），不是唯一的路；这种价值是“也许”最主要的（**perhaps its chief value**）。
items.en: Contemplation is one way of escape, and perhaps philosophy's chief value.

items.zh: “人是万物的尺度、真理是人造的”是罗素反对的观点，不是他自己的观点。
items.en: The view on which humanity is the measure of all things is one Russell rejects.

items.zh: 自我的扩大（**enlargement of the Self**）≠ 自私，它恰恰要求放下自我主张。
items.en: Enlarging the Self is not selfishness; it requires giving up self-assertion.

items.zh: **Self** 和 **not-Self** 首字母大写：自我＝认识者，非我＝被认识的整个世界。
items.en: Self is the knower; not-Self is the world known.

question.en: In Russell's image of a garrison in a beleaguered (besieged) fortress, what does the garrison stand for?
question.zh: 在罗素“被围困的要塞里的守军”这个意象中，守军代表什么？

options.en: The philosopher, who defends the truth against ignorant critics.
options.zh: 哲学家：替真理抵挡无知的批评者。

options.en: The life of the instinctive person, shut inside private interests and sure to be defeated by the great world outside.
options.zh: 本能式的人的生活：关在私人利益里，注定被外面的大世界打败。

options.en: Science, which is under attack from philosophy.
options.zh: 科学：正在受到哲学的攻击。

options.en: The free intellect, which sees the universe impartially.
options.zh: 自由的理智：不偏不倚地看宇宙。

explain.zh: 选 B（第 4 页）。守军代表只顾私人利益的本能式生活：处在一个迟早会毁掉它的大世界里，没有安宁。A、D 把它说成了哲学的生活，正好相反：哲学的沉思是逃出这座牢狱的一条路。C 读物里没有。
explain.en: B (p. 4). A and D describe the philosophic life, which is the way out; C is not in the reading.

title.zh: 罗素：自由的理智与“宇宙公民”
title.en: Russell: The Free Intellect and Citizenship of the Universe

blocks.zh: 真正的哲学沉思，以非我（**not-Self**）的每一次扩大为满足：凡是让被沉思的对象显得更大的东西，也让沉思的主体（**subject**，正在思考的“我”）变得更大（第 5 页）。反过来，沉思中一切个人的、私人的东西，一切依赖习惯、私利或欲望的东西，都会扭曲对象（**object**，被思考的东西），破坏理智追求的那种结合，变成理智的牢笼（第 5 页）。

items.en: intellect
items.zh: 理智
items.hint: 理解和推理的能力。

items.en: free intellect
items.zh: 自由的理智
items.hint: 不受私人希望、恐惧和习俗束缚，只想认识的心灵。

items.en: impartiality
items.zh: 不偏不倚
items.hint: 不站在自己这一边，也不站在任何一边。

items.en: abstract and universal knowledge
items.zh: 抽象而普遍的知识
items.hint: 不依赖某个人、某个地方、某个时刻的知识；个人经历的偶然进不去。

items.en: point of view
items.zh: 视角
items.hint: 从哪个人、哪个位置去看。

items.en: justice
items.zh: 正义
items.hint: 公平地对待每个人。

items.en: universal love
items.zh: 普遍的爱
items.hint: 能给所有人的爱，不只给有用或值得钦佩的人。

items.en: citizen of the universe
items.zh: 宇宙公民
items.hint: 把整个宇宙当成自己所属之处的人。

items.en: highest good
items.zh: 至善
items.hint: 最高的好，人最值得追求的东西。

items.en: speculation
items.zh: 思辨
items.hint: 对根本问题自由地去想、去推测。

items.en: dogmatic
items.zh: 独断的
items.hint: 不经检查就认定自己一定对。

items.en: standard form
items.zh: 标准形式
items.hint: 把论证（**argument**）的前提（**premise**）编号成 P1、P2……，最后写结论（**conclusion**）C。

items.en: objection
items.zh: 反驳
items.hint: 对一个论证提出的质疑。

title.zh: 自由的理智是什么样的（第 6 页）
title.en: What the free intellect is like (p. 6)

items.zh: 罗素说，自由的理智（**free intellect**）会 “as God might see”，像上帝可能看到的那样去看。
items.en: Russell says the free intellect sees things "as God might see" (p. 6).

items.zh: 没有“此时此地”：不从某个特定的地点、时刻出发去看。
items.en: It sees without a here and now.

items.zh: 没有希望和恐惧，也不受习惯信念和传统偏见的束缚。
items.en: It has no hopes and fears and is not bound by customary beliefs and traditional prejudices.

items.zh: 冷静、不动感情，只想要知识，而且是人类所能达到的最不带个人色彩的知识。
items.en: It is calm and dispassionate and wants only knowledge, as impersonal as humans can reach.

items.zh: 所以它更看重抽象而普遍（**abstract and universal**）的知识，因为个人经历的偶然进不去；不太看重感官知识，因为感官知识依赖一个个人的视角（**point of view**），依赖一个感官既揭示又扭曲的身体。
items.en: So it values abstract, universal knowledge more than knowledge from the senses, which depends on one person's point of view and on a body whose senses distort as much as they reveal.

blocks.zh: 注意（本站的理解）：“像上帝可能看到的那样去看”是一个比喻，意思是完全不偏不倚、不带个人立场地看；同一句话后面的解释（没有此时此地、没有希望和恐惧、只想要知识）说的就是这个。罗素在这里不是在讲宗教，也没有说上帝存在或人能变成上帝；而且他要的只是人类“所能达到的”最不带个人色彩的知识（第 6 页）。这和哈特说的“上帝的问题”是两回事（第 13 节）。
blocks.en: On this station's reading, seeing as God might see is a metaphor for impartial knowledge, as the rest of Russell's sentence explains; it is not a religious claim, and it differs from Hart's question of God.

blocks.zh: 像高考的“密封阅卷”：老师看不到考生的名字、学校、家乡，只看答案本身。去掉“这是谁的卷子”这些个人因素，判断就更公正。罗素的自由理智，就是对整个世界做这样的密封阅卷：不带“我在哪里、我想要什么、我怕什么”去看。
blocks.limit: 阅卷老师还是有自己的口味和视角；罗素也承认，人只能做到人类所能达到的程度。另外，阅卷是为了打分，而罗素说的沉思不为任何用处，只为知识本身。

headers: 同一种不偏不倚表现为
rows: 沉思（contemplation）
纯粹的求真愿望（**the unalloyed desire for truth**；unalloyed＝不掺杂质的）
只想知道真相，不掺私心
行动（action）
正义（**justice**）
把自己的目的和欲望只看成整体中极小的一部分，不再固执地坚持（罗素对行动和情感一起这样说）
情感（emotion）
普遍的爱（**universal love**）
能给所有人，不只给被认为有用或值得钦佩的人

caption.zh: 罗素说这是同一种心灵品质（第 6 页）
caption.en: Russell says this is one and the same quality of mind (p. 6)

blocks.zh: 习惯了哲学沉思那种自由和不偏不倚的心灵，在行动和情感的世界里也会保留一些：它把自己的目的和欲望看成整体的一部分，看成世界里极小的碎片，而世界的其余部分并不受任何一个人行为的影响（第 6 页）。所以沉思扩大的不只是思想的对象，还有行动和感情的对象：它让我们成为宇宙公民（**citizens of the universe**），而不只是一座有城墙、和其他所有城市交战的城的公民。人真正的自由，就在这种身份里（第 6 页）。

label.zh: 论证的标准形式（本站重构）：自由的理智与宇宙公民（第 5–6 页）
label.en: Standard form (our reconstruction): the free intellect and citizenship of the universe (pp. 5-6)

items.en: P1: Whatever is personal or private in contemplation, such as habit, self-interest or desire, distorts its object and damages the union the intellect seeks. (p. 5)
items.zh: P1：沉思中个人的、私人的东西，比如习惯、私利、欲望，会扭曲对象，破坏理智追求的结合。

items.en: P2: The free intellect knows impartially, without a personal here and now, without hopes and fears and without customary prejudices; so it values abstract, universal knowledge above sense-knowledge tied to one point of view. (pp. 5-6)
items.zh: P2：自由的理智不偏不倚地认识：没有个人的此时此地，没有希望和恐惧，没有习惯的偏见；所以它看重抽象普遍的知识，胜过依赖某一视角的感官知识。

items.en: P3: A mind used to this impartiality keeps some of it in action and emotion, seeing its own desires as tiny parts of the whole. (p. 6)
items.zh: P3：习惯了这种不偏不倚的心灵，在行动和情感中也会保留一些，把自己的欲望看成整体中极小的部分。

items.en: P4: The impartiality that is the pure desire for truth in contemplation is the same quality that is justice in action and universal love in emotion. (p. 6)
items.zh: P4：在沉思中是纯粹求真愿望的那种不偏不倚，和行动中的正义、情感中的普遍的爱，是同一种品质。

items.en: C: So contemplation enlarges the objects of our thoughts, actions and feelings and makes us citizens of the universe; in this lies our true freedom. (p. 6)
items.zh: C：所以沉思扩大了我们思想、行动和感情的对象，让我们成为宇宙公民；我们真正的自由就在这里。

label.zh: 论证的标准形式（本站重构）：罗素的总结（第 6–7 页）
label.en: Standard form (our reconstruction): Russell's final summary (pp. 6-7)

items.en: P1: As a rule, no definite answers to philosophical questions can be known to be true. (p. 6)
items.zh: P1：通常，哲学问题的确定答案都不能被知道为真。

items.en: P2: Philosophical questions widen our sense of what is possible, feed our intellectual imagination and weaken the dogmatic confidence that shuts the mind against speculation. (p. 6)
items.zh: P2：哲学问题扩大我们对“什么是可能的”的看法，丰富理智上的想象，削弱那种让心灵拒绝思辨的独断自信。

items.en: P3: Above all, by contemplating the greatness of the universe, the mind itself becomes great and capable of union with the universe, which is its highest good. (pp. 6-7)
items.zh: P3：最重要的是，通过沉思宇宙的伟大，心灵自己也变得伟大，能够和宇宙结合，这就是心灵的至善。

items.en: C: So philosophy should be studied not for definite answers but for the sake of the questions themselves. (pp. 6-7)
items.zh: C：所以学哲学不是为了确定的答案，而是为了问题本身。

prompt.en: Objection: 'Studying philosophy does not obviously make people more just or more loving. Many learned people are narrow and unfair.' How strong is this objection to Russell?
prompt.zh: 反驳：“学哲学并不明显让人更公正、更有爱，很多有学问的人也很狭隘、不公平。”这个反驳对罗素有多强？

answer.en: It is a serious objection, because the step from impartial contemplation to justice and universal love is a psychological claim that Russell does not support with evidence. However, his claim is modest: a mind used to impartial contemplation will keep some of that impartiality in action and emotion; he does not say every student becomes just. A fair assessment is that Russell describes what philosophy can do for someone who practises real contemplation, not what it always does.
answer.zh: 这是个有力的反驳：从“不偏不倚地沉思”到“正义和普遍的爱”，是一个关于人的心理的说法，罗素没有拿出证据。不过他的说法其实比较温和：习惯了不偏不倚沉思的心灵，会在行动和情感中保留“一些”这种品质（第 6 页），不是说每个学哲学的人都会变得公正。公平的评价是：罗素描述的是哲学“能够”为真正沉思的人做什么，而不是它“总是”做到什么。

prompt.en: Objection: 'Humans always see from a body, a place and a time. Nobody can know without a here and now, so Russell's free intellect is impossible.' How might Russell reply?
prompt.zh: 反驳：“人总是从一个身体、一个地点、一个时间去看，没有人能不带此时此地去认识，所以罗素说的自由理智不可能。”罗素可以怎样回应？

answer.en: Russell admits the limit: he asks for knowledge as impersonal as it is possible for humans to reach, not for a perfect view from no position at all. His picture of an impartial, God-like view is an ideal that guides us away from private hopes, fears and customs. Even if we never reach it fully, moving toward it can still reduce the distortions that come from habit, self-interest and desire, and that is all his argument needs.
answer.zh: 罗素自己承认有限度：他要的是人类“所能达到的”最不带个人色彩的知识（第 6 页），不是一个完全没有立场的视角。“像上帝那样看”是一个理想，引导我们远离私人的希望、恐惧和习俗。就算永远做不到完全，向它靠近也能减少习惯、私利和欲望造成的扭曲，这对罗素的论证就够了。

items.zh: “像上帝可能看到的那样”是比喻，表示不偏不倚，不是宗教主张。
items.en: Seeing as God might see is a metaphor for impartiality.

items.zh: 罗素更看重抽象普遍的知识，是因为它不受个人视角的影响，不是因为他看不起科学或经验。
items.en: Russell prefers abstract knowledge for its impartiality, not out of contempt for science.

items.zh: 宇宙公民（**citizens of the universe**）的对立面，是只做“一座有城墙、和其他所有城市交战的城”的公民。
items.en: The contrast is with being citizens only of a single walled city that fights all the others.

items.zh: 总结里罗素说的是“通常”（**as a rule**）没有确定答案能被知道为真，不是“永远不可能有答案”。
items.en: As a rule, not never.

items.zh: 总结有两部分：问题扩大可能性、丰富想象、减少独断；而“最重要的是”（**above all**）心灵因沉思宇宙的伟大而变得伟大，能和宇宙结合（至善）。
items.en: The summary has two parts, and the greatness of mind and union with the universe come above all.

question.en: For Russell, the impartiality that in contemplation is the pure desire for truth is, in action, ____ and, in emotion, ____.
question.zh: 罗素说，在沉思中是纯粹求真愿望的那种不偏不倚，在行动中是____，在情感中是____。

options.en: courage; pity
options.zh: 勇敢；怜悯

options.en: prudence; friendship
options.zh: 审慎；友谊

options.en: obedience; patriotism
options.zh: 服从；爱国

options.en: justice; universal love
options.zh: 正义；普遍的爱

explain.zh: 选 D（第 6 页）：同一种不偏不倚，在沉思中是纯粹的求真愿望，在行动中是正义，在情感中是能给所有人的普遍的爱。C 的“爱国”反而接近罗素不赞成的那种只做“一座有城墙、和其他所有城市交战的城”的公民的心态（本站的理解）；A、B 读物里都没有。
explain.en: D (p. 6). C is close to the walled-city attitude Russell rejects; A and B are not in the reading.

title.zh: 比较：哈特与罗素论惊奇和哲学的价值
title.en: Comparison: Hart and Russell on Wonder and the Value of Philosophy

blocks.zh: 这一节把两篇放在一起，方便写小论文（**short essay**）。它不对应某一篇的某几页，用到的是：哈特第 1–8 页（主要是第 1–4、7–8 页），罗素第 1–7 页（主要是第 1–4、6–7 页）。两篇都是第 2 周“敬畏与惊奇”的读物：哈特问惊奇揭示了关于实在的什么，属于形而上学（**metaphysics**：研究实在根本上是什么的学问）；罗素问哲学对学习者有什么价值。下面的比较是本站的整理（**interpretation**：本站的理解，不是作者的原话），每一点都标了读物页码。

items.en: absolute contingency
items.zh: 绝对偶然性
items.hint: 哈特：世界不必是这个样子，甚至根本不必存在。

items.en: ontological vs. aetiological
items.zh: 存在论的 vs. 因果的
items.hint: 哈特：问“为什么竟有东西存在” vs. 问物理原因、起源和成分。

items.en: tyranny of custom
items.zh: 习俗的暴政
items.hint: 罗素：没想过的习惯信念管住我们的思想。

items.en: dogmatism
items.zh: 独断
items.hint: 不经检查、傲慢地认定自己一定对。

items.en: contemplation / impartiality
items.zh: 沉思 / 不偏不倚
items.hint: 罗素：不为用处、不分敌我地看整个宇宙。

items.en: short essay
items.zh: 小论文
items.hint: 考试里要求写一段完整论述的题：论点、论证、反驳、回应、结论。

title.zh: 共同点
title.en: Where they agree

items.zh: 都在熟悉的东西里找惊奇：哈特说熟悉的一切突然显得怪异（第 2 页）；罗素说哲学把熟悉的东西用陌生的样子展示出来（第 4 页）。
items.en: Both find wonder in familiar things.

items.zh: 都把习惯当成惊奇的敌人：哈特的“习惯取代敬畏”（第 2 页），对应罗素的“习俗的暴政”（第 3 页）。
items.en: Both see habit or custom as the enemy of wonder.

items.zh: 都反对把深刻的问题草草打发：哈特批评那三种借口（第 3–4 页）；罗素批评只看物质需要、说哲学无用的人（第 1–2 页）。
items.en: Both reject brushing deep questions aside.

items.zh: 都认为没有确定答案的问题仍然值得问（哈特第 8 页；罗素第 6–7 页）。
items.en: Both value questions without settled answers.

title.zh: 不同点
title.en: Where they differ

items.zh: 惊奇的对象：哈特是存在本身（为什么竟有东西存在）；罗素是宇宙的伟大和各种可能性。
items.en: Object of wonder: existence itself vs. the greatness of the universe and new possibilities.

items.zh: 有多确定：哈特说那一瞬间是对一个真理（世界绝对偶然）的真实一瞥（第 4 页）；罗素说确定的答案通常不能被知道为真（第 6 页）。
items.en: Confidence: a glimpse of a truth vs. no definite answers known as a rule.

items.zh: 走向哪里：哈特走向上帝的问题（第 8 页）；罗素走向不偏不倚的沉思、正义、普遍的爱，以及和宇宙的结合（第 4–7 页）。
items.en: Destination: the question of God vs. impartial contemplation, justice, universal love and union with the universe.

items.zh: 问的问题：哈特关心惊奇揭示了关于实在的什么；罗素关心哲学对学习者的人生有什么好处。
items.en: Question: what wonder reveals about reality vs. what philosophy does for the student.

label.zh: 考试这样写：比较哈特和罗素
label.en: Exam sentences: comparing Hart and Russell

items.en: Both Hart and Russell link philosophy to wonder at familiar things, and both see habit or custom as the enemy of wonder.
items.zh: 哈特和罗素都把哲学和对熟悉事物的惊奇联系起来，也都认为习惯或习俗是惊奇的敌人。

items.en: For Hart, wonder is about existence itself: that anything exists at all. For Russell, wonder comes from seeing new possibilities and the greatness of the universe.
items.zh: 对哈特来说，惊奇针对存在本身：竟然有东西存在。对罗素来说，惊奇来自看见新的可能性和宇宙的伟大。

items.en: Hart claims that the experience of wonder gives a real glimpse of a truth, the world's absolute contingency, while Russell holds that definite answers usually cannot be known to be true.
items.zh: 哈特认为惊奇的体验让人真实地瞥见一个真理，即世界的绝对偶然性；罗素则认为确定的答案通常不能被知道为真。

items.en: Hart's reflection leads to the question of God, which he says differs in kind from questions about the gods; Russell mentions God only as an image of impartial knowledge.
items.zh: 哈特的思考走向上帝的问题，他说这和关于诸神的问题在种类上不同；罗素提到上帝，只是把它当成不偏不倚的知识的比喻。

items.en: Both value questions that may never be answered: Hart because reason cannot leave the mystery of existence alone, Russell because the questions free and enlarge the mind.
items.zh: 两人都重视也许永远没有答案的问题：哈特是因为理性放不下存在之谜，罗素是因为这些问题让心灵自由、广大。

text.en: Contemplation makes us citizens of the universe.

text.en: Children may be more open to the sheer givenness of the world.
text.zh: 小孩子也许更能敞开地感受到世界就这样被给予。

why.zh: 哈特第 1–2 页（没有“为什么”的玫瑰）。

text.en: Philosophy's value is indirect, through its effects on those who study it.
text.zh: 哲学的价值是间接的，通过它对学习者的影响实现。

why.zh: 罗素第 1 页。

text.en: Wonder goes with seeing familiar things as strange or unfamiliar.
text.zh: 惊奇和“把熟悉的东西看成陌生的”连在一起。

text.zh: 每个有限的东西每时每刻都依赖自身之外的东西。

text.en: Self-assertion is an obstacle to the growth of the Self.
text.zh: 自我主张会阻碍自我的成长。

why.zh: 罗素第 4–5 页。

text.en: Brushing a deep question aside as meaningless or useless is a mistake.
text.zh: 把深刻的问题当成没意义、没用而打发掉，是错误的。

why.zh: 哈特批评把存在的问题说成语法错误或说不通（第 4 页）；罗素批评只看物质需要、说哲学无用的人（第 1–2 页）。

title.zh: 小论文提纲：比较哈特和罗素论惊奇
title.en: Short-essay outline: Hart and Russell on wonder

items.en: Thesis: both tie philosophy to wonder at the familiar, but they disagree about what wonder reveals and where it leads.
items.zh: 论点：两人都把哲学和对熟悉事物的惊奇联系起来，但对惊奇揭示了什么、通向哪里看法不同。

items.en: Hart: wonder is about existence itself; give his argument (what vs. that, absolute contingency, ontological not merely aetiological) and Taylor's sphere.
items.zh: 哈特：惊奇针对存在本身；写出他的论证（是什么与存在着、绝对偶然、存在论而不只是因果）和泰勒的圆球。

items.en: Russell: philosophy's value lies in uncertainty and in contemplating the universe; give his argument (tyranny of custom, what things may be, Self and not-Self).
items.zh: 罗素：哲学的价值在不确定性和对宇宙的沉思；写出他的论证（习俗的暴政、事物可能是什么、自我与非我）。

items.en: Agreement: habit or custom is the enemy; unanswered questions are still worth asking.
items.zh: 共同点：习惯或习俗是敌人；没有答案的问题仍然值得问。

items.en: Difference: Hart claims a glimpse of a truth and raises the question of God; Russell stresses possibilities rather than definite answers and uses God only as an image of impartiality.
items.zh: 不同点：哈特说瞥见了一个真理并提出上帝的问题；罗素强调的是可能性而不是确定的答案，并且只把上帝当作不偏不倚的比喻。

items.en: Assessment: for example, Hart's hidden premise that contingent existence needs an explanation vs. Russell's unsupported claim that impartiality becomes justice and love.
items.zh: 评价：例如哈特的隐含前提（偶然的存在需要解释）对比罗素缺少证据的说法（不偏不倚会变成正义和爱）。

items.en: Conclusion: one sentence on which view you find stronger and why.
items.zh: 结论：用一句话说你觉得哪一方更有说服力、为什么。

prompt.en: Compare Hart and Russell on the role of wonder in philosophy. Where do they agree, and where do they differ?
prompt.zh: 比较哈特和罗素对惊奇在哲学中作用的看法：他们哪里一致，哪里不同？

answer.en: Both Hart and Russell link philosophy to wonder at familiar things, and both say that habit or custom kills that wonder. They also agree that some questions are worth asking even if they cannot be answered. But for Hart wonder is a glimpse of a truth about existence, the world's absolute contingency, and it leads to the question of God. For Russell wonder is kept alive by philosophy's uncertainty, which shows what things may be, and it leads to impartial contemplation, justice and union with the universe.
answer.zh: 先写共同点（熟悉事物中的惊奇、习惯是敌人、无解的问题值得问），再写三个不同（惊奇的对象、有多确定、走向哪里）。每一点后面最好带上页码或例子（玫瑰、泰勒的圆球、天文学、要塞守军）：用读物里的具体内容支持比较，最能拿分。

prompt.en: Which author gives the stronger case for valuing questions without definite answers? Defend one view briefly.
prompt.zh: 哪位作者更有力地说明了没有确定答案的问题值得重视？简要为一方辩护。

answer.en: Russell's case is more modest and so easier to defend: he claims only that philosophical questions widen our sense of what is possible and free us from dogmatism, which readers can test in their own experience. Hart claims more, that a brief experience reveals a deep truth about reality, and this rests on the hidden premise that contingent existence needs an explanation. On the other hand, Hart explains why the question of existence cannot be removed by progress in science, while Russell's claim that impartial contemplation produces justice and universal love is unsupported. A good answer picks one side and admits the other's strength.
answer.zh: 两边都可以选，关键是有理由。支持罗素：他的说法温和，可以在自己身上检验。支持哈特：他说明了为什么存在的问题不会因为科学进步而消失。不管选谁，都要承认对方的长处，并点出自己这一方的弱点（哈特的隐含前提；罗素关于心理迁移的说法缺证据）。

items.zh: 罗素的“像上帝可能看到的那样去看”是比喻；哈特的“上帝的问题”是一个真问题。别说“两人都在谈上帝存在”。
items.en: Russell's God is a metaphor; Hart's question of God is a real question.

items.zh: 哈特说那一瞬间是对真理的真实一瞥；罗素说确定的答案通常不能被知道为真。别说“两人都认为惊奇只是一种感觉”。
items.en: Hart claims a glimpse of truth; Russell claims no definite answers as a rule.

items.zh: “习惯取代敬畏”是哈特的说法，“习俗的暴政”是罗素的说法。意思相近，引用时别张冠李戴。
items.en: Habit displacing awe is Hart's phrase; the tyranny of custom is Russell's.

items.zh: 两人都重视没有答案的问题，但理由不同：哈特说理性面对存在之谜停不下来；罗素说问题能让心灵自由、广大。
items.en: Both value unanswered questions, for different reasons.

blocks.zh: 以后复习可以连起来看（本站的联想）：罗素说的“我们开头几章”，包括第 7 周读的《哲学问题》第 1–2 章（桌子的颜色）；第 8 周休谟说习惯（**custom or habit**）是人生的伟大向导，可以和罗素反对“习俗的暴政”、哈特说“习惯取代敬畏”对照；第 9 周内格尔强调经验离不开视角（**point of view**），正好和罗素想要的没有“此时此地”的自由理智形成张力。

question.en: Which statement is true of BOTH Hart and Russell?
question.zh: 下面哪一句对哈特和罗素都成立？

options.en: Both say that habit or custom dulls our wonder at familiar things.
options.zh: 两人都说习惯或习俗会磨掉我们对熟悉事物的惊奇。

options.en: Both argue that reflection on contingency must raise the question of God.
options.zh: 两人都论证：思考偶然性一定会碰到上帝的问题。

options.en: Both claim that philosophy's value lies in its usefulness to people who never study it.
options.zh: 两人都说哲学的价值在于对从不学它的人有用。

options.en: Both hold that the question of existence is aetiological.
options.zh: 两人都认为存在的问题是因果的问题。

explain.zh: 选 A：哈特说习惯取代敬畏（第 2 页）；罗素说没有哲学的人被习惯信念关住，常见的东西引不起他的问题，而哲学让惊奇保持活力（第 3–4 页）。B 只是哈特的观点（第 8 页）。C 与罗素正好相反：他说哲学没有这种效用（第 1 页）。D 与哈特相反：他说存在的问题是存在论的，不只是因果的（第 4 页）。
explain.en: A (Hart p. 2; Russell pp. 3-4). B is only Hart's view; C contradicts Russell (p. 1); D contradicts Hart (p. 4).

summary.en: Hart, following Plato and Aristotle, argues that philosophy begins in wonder, and he extends this to all serious thought that is not merely calculative or appetitive.
summary.zh: 哈特沿着柏拉图和亚里士多德的说法，认为哲学开始于惊奇，并把这一点推广到一切不只是算计或欲求的认真思考。

summary.en: For Hart, wonder is not curiosity about a missing fact; it is the sudden awareness that no fact could explain the mystery that anything exists at all.
summary.zh: 在哈特看来，惊奇不是对缺少的某个事实的好奇，而是突然意识到：任何事实都解释不了“竟然有东西存在”这个谜。

summary.en: Hart suggests that small children may sense the world's givenness more openly, but adults let habit replace awe, so the experience returns only in rare moments.
summary.zh: 哈特认为小孩子也许更能敞开地感受到世界的被给予，大人却让习惯取代了敬畏，所以这种体验只在很少的瞬间回来。

summary.en: In those moments we see that what a thing is (its essence) never explains that it is (its existence): nothing has the power to give itself existence.
summary.zh: 在那些瞬间我们看到：一个东西“是什么”（本质）永远解释不了它“存在着”（存在）；没有东西有让自己存在的能力。

summary.en: People explain this ontological surprise away as a brain glitch like déjà vu, or dismiss the question of existence as a confusion of grammar or as unintelligible; Hart replies that these moves give up the responsibility to think.
summary.zh: 人们把这种存在论的惊讶说成像似曾相识那样的大脑故障，或者把存在的问题说成语法造成的混乱、根本说不通；哈特回应说，这些做法是在推卸思考的责任。

summary.en: Hart argues that the experience reveals the world's absolute contingency: the world could have been different, and it could have not existed at all.
summary.zh: 哈特论证：这种体验揭示了世界的绝对偶然性，世界本来可以是别的样子，也本来可以根本不存在。

summary.en: For Hart the mystery is ontological, not merely aetiological: physical explanations deal with origins, earlier states, persistence and parts, but only by other contingent things, so they never explain why anything exists.
summary.zh: 对哈特来说，这个谜是存在论的，不只是因果的：物理的解释处理起源、之前的状态、持续和成分，但只能用别的偶然之物来解释，所以永远解释不了为什么竟有东西存在。

summary.en: Taylor's sphere shows that a rock, a tree, or a sphere as big as the universe or lasting forever raises the same question of existence; only familiarity stops us from asking it.
summary.zh: 泰勒的圆球说明：一块石头、一棵树，或者像宇宙那么大、永远存在的圆球，都提出同样的存在问题；只是因为熟悉，我们才不问。

summary.en: Hart's ontological poverty means that every finite thing depends at every moment on things outside itself, so nothing in nature has the ground of its being within itself.
summary.zh: 哈特说的存在上的贫乏是指：每个有限的东西每时每刻都依赖自身之外的东西，所以自然中没有任何东西在自身之内拥有存在的根据。

summary.en: Hart says that any deep reflection on contingency must raise the question of God, which differs in kind from questions about the gods within nature, but he does not prove that God exists.
summary.zh: 哈特说，任何深入思考偶然性的人都一定会碰到上帝的问题，这个问题和关于自然之内诸神的问题在种类上不同；但他没有证明上帝存在。

summary.en: Russell argues that philosophy, unlike science, is not useful to people who never study it; its value is indirect, through its effects on its students, and it lies among the goods of the mind.
summary.zh: 罗素论证：哲学不像科学那样对不学它的人有用；它的价值是间接的，通过它对学习者的影响实现，而且在心灵的好处之中。

summary.en: Russell argues that philosophy looks uncertain partly because questions that can be answered definitely become separate sciences, such as astronomy and psychology, so philosophy is the residue that is left (the station calls this the residue argument).
summary.zh: 罗素论证：哲学看起来不确定，部分是因为能确定回答的问题都变成了独立的科学，比如天文学和心理学，留下的剩余部分才叫哲学（本站把这个论证叫“剩余物”论证）。

summary.en: Russell also admits that some deep questions may be insoluble, but he says philosophy must keep them alive so that our speculative interest in the universe does not die.
summary.zh: 罗素也承认有些深刻的问题也许无解，但他说哲学必须让它们保持活力，免得我们对宇宙的思辨兴趣死掉。

summary.en: Russell argues that the value of philosophy lies largely in its uncertainty: it frees us from the tyranny of custom, removes arrogant dogmatism and keeps wonder alive by making familiar things look new.
summary.zh: 罗素论证：哲学的价值在很大程度上就在它的不确定性中：它把我们从习俗的暴政中解放出来，去掉傲慢的独断，并通过让熟悉的东西显得新鲜来保持惊奇。

summary.en: Russell says that contemplating the greatness of the universe enlarges the Self and frees us from narrow private aims; its impartiality becomes justice in action and universal love in emotion and makes us citizens of the universe.
summary.zh: 罗素说，沉思宇宙的伟大能扩大自我，让我们摆脱狭隘的私人目标；这种不偏不倚在行动中成为正义，在情感中成为普遍的爱，让我们成为宇宙公民。

summary.en: Russell concludes that philosophy should be studied for the sake of its questions, not for definite answers.
summary.zh: 罗素的结论是：学哲学是为了它的问题，而不是为了确定的答案。

examFocus.en: Define Hart's wonder and contrast it with curiosity.
examFocus.zh: 本站估计可能出选择题：好奇缺的是一个事实，惊奇是任何事实都解释不了的存在之谜。

examFocus.en: Explain essence ('what it is') versus existence ('that it is') and why Hart says the first never explains the second.
examFocus.zh: 本站估计可能出简答题：这是一个概念区分，也是哈特核心论证的第一个前提。

examFocus.en: List the three ways of explaining away ontological surprise, give Hart's reply, and assess whether a feeling can count as evidence.
examFocus.zh: 本站估计简答和小论文都可能考：三种借口加哈特的回应，再加上“感觉不是证据”的评价。

examFocus.en: Explain the ontological versus aetiological distinction, put Hart's core argument in standard form, and raise the objection that the universe might exist with no explanation at all.
examFocus.zh: 本站估计这是全周最可能出小论文的一题：标准形式加隐含前提加反驳。

examFocus.en: Explain Taylor's sphere and what the size and duration variants are meant to show.
examFocus.zh: 本站估计可能考这个例子：圆球想说明什么、为什么大小和时间无关。

examFocus.en: Define ontological poverty and explain the objection that what holds of every part need not hold of the whole.
examFocus.zh: 本站估计选择题可能拿“贫乏”的字面意思做干扰项；评价题可能考“每一部分都依赖，推不出整体也依赖”这个问题。

examFocus.en: Describe Hart's three directions of reflection, beings versus being as such, and his claim about the question of God, noting that he gives no proof.
examFocus.zh: 本站提醒的陷阱：哈特没有证明上帝存在；诸神和上帝不同。

examFocus.en: Explain why Russell says philosophy's value is indirect and lies among the goods of the mind.
examFocus.zh: 本站估计可能出选择题：科学的效用和哲学的间接价值的对比。

examFocus.en: Explain the residue argument (the station's name for Russell's point on p. 2) with astronomy and psychology, and give Russell's three possibly insoluble questions.
examFocus.zh: 本站估计选择题可能考两个例子和三个问题；简答可能要你写出论证（“剩余物”论证是本站起的名字）。

examFocus.en: Explain why Russell says philosophy's value lies largely in its uncertainty: prejudice, the tyranny of custom, and knowledge of what things may be.
examFocus.zh: 罗素这篇的核心论点之一，本站估计简答和小论文都可能考。

examFocus.en: Explain the garrison image, Self and not-Self, self-assertion, and the view Russell rejects, on which humanity is the measure of all things.
examFocus.zh: 本站估计可能考这些意象和概念；注意分清罗素自己的观点和他反对的观点。

examFocus.en: Explain the free intellect, impartiality as justice and universal love, citizenship of the universe, and Russell's final summary.
examFocus.zh: 本站估计选择题可能考“正义、普遍的爱”这一对；罗素的总结适合用在小论文里。

examFocus.en: Compare Hart and Russell on wonder: two agreements and two differences, with examples from both readings.
examFocus.zh: 本站估计期末小论文可能要求比较两篇读物。
